provenance.source: Lei 7.713/1988 e Lei 15.270/2025 (Reforma da Renda); tabela INSS 2026; tabela IRRF mensal; PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Brazil
provenance.notes: The 2026 INSS table was read on 31 August 2026 and reconciles exactly: 8.475,55 x 14% - 198,49 = 988,09, the published maximum. The R$ 5.000 exemption and the redutor formula came from Brazilian summaries of the Reforma da Renda. PwC's own page still showed a 2024 table and was not used.

omissions: Legal deductions for dependants, alimony, private pension and health plans are not modelled; the simplified discount is applied instead.
The 13th salary is taxed separately and exclusively at source in Brazil, which this app does not model.
The annual adjustment declaration, which can change the result, is not modelled; this sums the monthly withholding basis.

inss.note: Progressive by band, applied to the whole salary with a deduction amount. It stops at the ceiling, so the maximum contribution is R$ 988,09 a month no matter how much you earn.

irrfMonthly.note: Brazil withholds monthly on a monthly table, so the tax is genuinely a sum of twelve separate computations rather than one annual calculation.

simplifiedDiscount.note: A flat monthly discount that replaces all legal deductions. You take it or your actual deductions, never both.

reformaDaRenda.note: From 2026 monthly pay up to R$ 5.000 bears no income tax at all, and between R$ 5.000 and R$ 7.350 a redutor reduces the tax on a sliding scale that reaches zero exactly at the ceiling.

regions.name: Brasil
regions.note: Brazilian income tax on wages has no state or municipal component.

inputSchema.label: Salario bruto (per month)
inputSchema.help: Gross monthly salary. Brazil computes INSS and income tax on each month separately, so the monthly figures matter here more than in almost any other country on this list.

inputSchema.label: IRRF retido (per month)
inputSchema.help: Income tax withheld each month, for the annual comparison.
